description: Polelit is a Buenos Aires team on the CLPS Lunar Mission Browser challenge. We are building an intuitive web app to compare landing sites and dates at the lunar south pole, showing the Sun and Earth above the horizon to assess solar power and communication with Earth. We combine aerospace engineering, Python and web app development. Looking for UI/UX design and video skills.
summary: Polelit ("the lit pole") is a web tool that shows the Sun and the Earth over the real horizon of four lunar south pole landing sites, hour by hour during 2027. At the south pole the Sun never rises more than a few degrees, so nearby terrain can leave a site dark for days and block direct communication with Earth. Polelit lets mission planners, educators and the public compare sites and dates at a glance. It recommends a site based on energy, communication or a balance of both, shows how long until the Sun and the Earth set, finds the best landing window and compares two dates.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Polelit is a web tool for choosing where and when to land at the lunar south pole. For four sites, it shows the Sun and the Earth over the real horizon, hour by hour during 2027.

- Mission planner: choose a priority (energy, communication or balanced) and get a recommended site, with the four sites compared using color tags.

- View from the lander: the 360° horizon with the Sun and the Earth on top.

- Time navigation: move through 2027 hour by hour or pick a landing day.

- Countdowns: time until sunset and until the Earth hides or appears.

- Best landing window: the longest period with the Sun and the Earth visible at the same time.

- Compare two dates: useful when a launch slips.

- Educator view and technical view, in English and Spanish.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Sun and Earth positions come from the NASA JPL Horizons API, every hour of 2027, for an observer 2 m above the ground.

2. The horizon is computed from the LOLA 80 m elevation map, in 360 directions up to 150 km, including the curvature of the Moon.

3. The Sun is treated as a disk, so the visible fraction is computed.

4. Slope comes from the LOLA 5 m maps and distance to permanent shadow from the LOLA 20 m map.

5. Results are saved as JSON files read by the website.

RESULTS (2027)

- Shackleton–de Gerlache Ridge: 88.2% sunlight, best for energy.

- Malapert Massif: 72.0% Earth in view, best for communication.

VALIDATION

Mean sunlight on the ridge: 88.2% (ours) vs 88.0% (Gläser et al., 2017). Longest night on the Shackleton rim: 64 h vs 65 h.

IMPACT

Mission planners can quickly re-evaluate sites and dates when plans change, and educators can show why the lunar south pole is so challenging.

TOOLS

Python, NumPy, Rasterio, Requests, Matplotlib, FastAPI, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js.

Code: https://github.com/wenndylimachi5-max/POLELIT
